name: Nestboard
whatItDoes: A shared board where a household keeps its chores, bills and groceries in one place: who does which chore this week, which bill is due and who pays it, and what is on the shopping list.
audience: Couples, families and housemates who run one home together and split its chores, bills and shopping between them.
problem: The running of the home lives in one person's head and in a scatter of notes, group chats and reminders, so chores are forgotten, bills are paid late and the same person ends up carrying it all.
differentiation: One board for the whole household: every chore, bill and grocery item has an owner and a date that everyone in the home sees.
alternatives: A paper chore chart on the fridge, the family group chat, a shared calendar, sticky notes, or one person who remembers everything.
proof: No result, review, user count or number of the product exists. One fact the customer supplies for its content: washing twelve place settings of dishes by hand took 103 litres of water on average across 113 people in seven European countries, against about 15 litres for a full load in a modern dishwasher. Source: Stamminger and others, University of Bonn, A European Comparison of Cleaning Dishes by Hand, 2003.
pricing: Not set. The customer is invented for a test.
voice: Warm, plain and a little dry, like one housemate talking to another. It never preaches and never blames.
constraints: TEST CUSTOMER, INVENTED ON 2026-10-04. Nestboard is not a real company. It has no real users, results, reviews, prices, website or logo: claim none of them. The website address is a reserved placeholder. Its brand colour, teal, was chosen for the test. Its mark (a flat teal house with a white tick) is a stand-in drawn for the test, not a real logo.

features.name: Chore board
features.whatItDoes: Lists this week's chores, each with one owner and a day, seen by everyone in the home.

features.name: Bills
features.whatItDoes: Shows which bill is due next and who pays it; reminders are not sent yet.

features.name: Shared grocery list
features.whatItDoes: One shopping list the whole household adds to and ticks off in the shop.

product.mainFlow: A person creates a home, invites the others by link, and adds the first chores; the board then shows who does what this week.
